LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 9.1.1 PRONUNCIATION: CONSONANT AND VOWEL SOUNDS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.1: Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant and Vowel Sounds
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant and Vowel Sounds, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should you pronounce words correctly? 2. Why do people find it difficult to pronounce some words? 3. In what ways can one improve own pronunciation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. articulate correctly the consonant sounds/t/, /d/, /l/, /r/ in words articulate correctly vowel sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ in words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant and Vowel Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. pronounce words correctly using stress,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant and Vowel Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. distinguish the meaning of words based on stress,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant and Vowel Sounds in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of correct pronunciation in oral communication.  Listen to audio clips and watch video clips with the sounds /t/, /d/, /l/, /r, /, /ʊ/ and /uː/ in words. Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing.  Articulate the following consonants and vowel sounds: - /t/ as in toll - /d/as in doll - /l/ as in liver - /r/ as in river - /ʊ/ as in pull, bull; - /uː/ as in pool, boot Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views. 1. Why should you pronounce words correctly? 2. Why do people find it difficult to pronounce some words? 3. In what ways can one improve own pronunciation? 83  Watch an oral presentation and pick out words with the target sounds. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Practise pronouncing words with the target consonant and vowel sounds, in pairs,  Sort words based on the pronunciation of the target, consonant, and vowel sounds  Recite poems or sing songs on national heroes with the target sounds,  Say tongue twisters with the target consonant and vowel sounds,  Listen to audio featuring a variety of words and classify them in their word classes according to the stressed syllables, 84  Engage in pronunciation drills on stress for distinguishing word class,  Underline stressed syllables in words  Discuss the importance of correct pronunciation and use of stress in conveying meaning,  Reflect on the target consonant and vowel sounds and identify those they struggle with for further practise.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation: Consonant and Vowel Sounds together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner listens to audio clips and watches videos on pronunciation of the vowel and

consonant sounds.

Learning to learn is emphasised as the learner practises the vowel and consonant sounds that they find difficult to pronounce.

Values:
 Patriotism as the learner inculcates the love for own country while reciting poems on nationalism.

 Unity is enhanced as the learner strives to achieve common goals while practising to recite and sing songs on nationalism

with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Patriotism and Good Governance are enhanced as the learner sings songs and recites poems on national heroes/ heroines with the

target vowel and consonant sounds.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of pronunciation with other language learning areas such as Kiswahili.
